name: # The LIVE cross-port divergence ledger -- the AUTHORITATIVE list.
# DIVERGENCE.md at the repository root explains the shape of these
# disagreements and points here; this file is what actually RUNS, so if
# the two ever disagree, this one wins.
# Six tab-separated columns. `go` and `ts` are what each port ACTUALLY
# produces today, as JSON, or ERROR:<code>. `opts` is a JSON object of
# make() options, or `-` for a stock parser.
# Every row is asserted by BOTH runners: the Go runner must reproduce the
# `go` column and the TS runner the `ts` column, on every run. So a
# divergence that gets FIXED fails this suite as loudly as one that
# regresses, and the row must then be deleted. That is the whole point —
# go/doc/differences.md is prose, and prose rots: through this session it
# claimed 2.e3 and 1e999 still diverged for some time after they were
# aligned, and claimed base-prefixed overflow was aligned before it was.
# A ledger nothing executes is documentation, not a gate.
# Adding a row here is an admission of parity debt, not a way to silence a
# failure. Fix the divergence if you can; record it here only when you
# cannot, with a justification a reader can act on.
string-replace-control
justification: TS string.replace can map a control character to a replacement, making it legal string body. The Go string matcher rejects the raw control character before replacement is consulted, reporting unprintable. (go/doc/differences.md said unterminated_string; this ledger caught that on its first run — the prose predated the error-code alignment.) Replacement of PRINTABLE characters is aligned (see the control row below), and the unprintable error scan does honour replace mappings when locating the first offending character — only this legality question differs.

name: string-replace-printable
justification: Control row, not a divergence: printable replacement is aligned. Kept adjacent so a fix to the row above cannot be mistaken for a regression here.

name: # --- Downstream of engine defects, added 2026-08-19 ------------------------
# Measured with scripts/parity-probe.sh, not authored. All six are live in
# this repo and were absent from this ledger while it described itself as
# the AUTHORITATIVE list -- three whole classes the audit had already named
# (U1, U3/U4, U5). Each cites the engine PR that closes it; when that lands,
# the row goes red and must be deleted.
text-ender-bare-quote
justification: Audit U1 (engine P1/P2). The text matcher's ender set omits the string quote characters in Go, so a quote ENDS a text run there and does not here: Go reaches the string matcher and reports an unterminated string, TypeScript keeps the quote inside the text value. ~2/3 of the 1,612 divergences in this repo's own 6,000-case fuzz run were this shape. Engine repair: tabnas/parser#128 — this row goes red on adoption, which is the signal to delete it.

name: text-ender-quote-in-text
justification: Same defect as text-ender-bare-quote, inside a map value rather than at the top level. Kept separate because the two reach the string matcher through different rules, and a partial fix could close one and not the other.

name: text-ender-quote-after-value
justification: Same defect after a NUMBER-shaped text run. TypeScript's value is the string "1\"", not the number 1, which is worth seeing: the divergence changes the TYPE of the parsed value, not only whether it parses.

name: line-separator-bare
justification: Audit U5 (engine P4). JavaScript's `.` excludes four line terminators and RE2's excludes one, so a text run crosses U+2028 in Go and does not here. NOTE: the input holds a RAW U+2028, invisible in an editor. It cannot be written \u2028 — the shared loader decodes only \n \r \t \\. The `go` column is its own sentinel: lose the character and Go yields {"a":"xy"}, so the row fails rather than silently testing something else. Engine repair: tabnas/parser#125.

name: paragraph-separator-bare
justification: As line-separator-bare, for U+2029. Both are pinned because the engine fix routes them through one byte-table entry (0xE2) and a repair that handled only one would leave this red.

name: malformed-unicode-escape
justification: Audit U3/U4 (engine P3). `parseInt` used as a validator stops at the first non-hex character and returns what it read, so TypeScript ACCEPTS this and emits a character that was never in the input — the `st` is consumed and discarded. Go rejects. This is a correctness bug in the canonical port on its own terms, not merely a divergence. Engine repair: tabnas/parser#123.
